content.text: Sessions on web_desktop fell about 57% starting at 12:00, just after a gtm-web tracking tag publish at 11:50. I'll check whether the drop is confined to desktop and whether orders held up.

The discount rate stepped up from about 6% to about 16% around 2026-08-28 06:00, across every category and channel. My earlier change-log query started at 08:00, so I'll check the hours before the step for a coupon entry.

The jump starts at 12:00, right after a `gtm-web` tracking-tag publish at 11:50 on web_desktop. I'll check whether sessions or revenue moved too, to tell a measurement change from a real conversion change.
The drop is concentrated on provider psp_beta. The PL-scoped change log shows no provider change, so I'll check provider-status entries across all countries.

input.summary: Desktop sessions ran 5-12% above expected from 10:00 to 15:00 on 2026-10-02 (peak 5818 vs 5263 expected at 12:00). The excess is concentrated in FR (+917 excess sessions over 4 hours), DE and ES, and spread across organic, direct, affiliate and paid channels rather than one channel, so it does not match the bot-traffic signature. Checkout conversion dipped at 12:00-13:00 but order volume stayed near expected. No calendar event explains it. The only change in scope is CHG-01851, a tax-tables config update at 10:54, which does not plausibly add sessions. Not established: the source of the extra traffic. Recommend the on-call check traffic sources in FR/DE/ES. No mitigation proposed.

Payment success for PL card fell from about 0.91 to 0.32 at 14:00 on 2026-08-05 and stayed low (0.35 at 15:00, 0.39 at 16:00). Breakdown for PL card from 14:00 to 17:00 shows the drop sits entirely in provider psp_beta: 0.35 versus a baseline of 0.910, on 60 attempts. Other providers in PL card were stable or up. No provider_status change was logged, and no change-log entry fits, so the cause is inferred from the breakdown and not confirmed. Not established: the provider-side error and whether psp_beta is failing in other countries. The failover to another provider for PL card is the suggested step.

From 12:00 UTC on 2026-10-01, web_desktop checkout_conversion jumped from about 0.056 to 0.151 (expected ~0.055), in all six countries. Sessions fell about 57% (4,821 at 11:00 to 2,105 at 12:00, versus ~4,960 expected), while net revenue rose about 22% above expected (35,768 vs 29,246). The only web_desktop change nearby is CHG-01830, a gtm-web container v231 publish with a new consent mode at 11:50. The likely reading is that the tag change undercounts sessions, not that checkout improved. This is inferred from timing and the session drop; I did not verify the tag's contents. No mitigation is proposed, since none is defined for tracking outages.

PL card payment success fell from about 0.91 to 0.32-0.39 starting 14:00 on 2026-08-05 and stayed low through 16:00. The breakdown shows the drop is on provider psp_beta (window 0.35 vs baseline 0.91, excess -33.6 payments). Other providers in the same window are flat or up (psp_alpha 0.936, psp_gamma 0.958), and psp_beta is only slightly down across all countries (0.877 vs 0.911), so the failure is concentrated in PL. No provider-status or other change-log entry explains it, so the cause is inferred from the signature, not confirmed. Recommend failing PL card traffic over from psp_beta and checking psp_beta's status with the provider.

Web_desktop sessions dropped about 57% from 12:00 on 2026-10-01 (2105 vs ~4960 expected, still ~1926 at 14:00). Other platforms moved within noise. Net revenue on web_desktop rose above expected over the same hours, so orders did not fall. The only change on web_desktop shortly before the drop is CHG-01830, a gtm-web container v231 publish at 11:50 with a new consent mode. This points to a tracking outage: sessions are under-recorded, not lost. Not established: the exact mechanism of the consent change, and whether real traffic moved. No mitigation proposed, since tracking outages have no automated fix.

Whole-business discount_rate ran about 2-3% above expected from 2026-09-05 ~10:00 to 14:00 (e.g. 0.0629 vs 0.0612 expected at 10:00, 0.0640 vs 0.0612 at 11:00), on volume near normal. The move is small. Change log shows a KIDS10 usage-limit raise at 13:12 and a mail-winback audience update at 14:24, but neither obviously explains a broad rise starting around 10:00. Breakdowns by channel and country show uniform shifts, but their baseline week (2026-08-29) reads about 0.16 discount rate, inconsistent with the expected series, so I did not rely on them. No cause established; recommend checking the coupon-usage and discount-application data for 09-05 morning directly.

NL paid_search sessions tripled from 11:00 on 2026-09-24 (1,218 at 11:00 and 1,446 at 12:00, vs ~380-430 expected), spread across all four platforms. Checkout conversion fell from ~0.054 to 0.017 over the same hours, so order count stayed roughly flat (~21-25 per hour vs ~18-21 expected). That pattern fits bot traffic on one channel and country. No change-log entry explains the surge: the nearest changes (android-5.1.7 at 08:28, feature-flags at 11:09, coupon GARTEN15 at 12:14) do not fit its place or timing. The bot inference is from the traffic pattern only; I did not confirm the source of the traffic.

iOS checkout conversion fell from about 6.0% to 2.7% starting 08:00 on 2026-08-18 (expected about 6.2%). The drop appears in all six countries, while Android and web are flat. Release ios-7.3.0 (CHG-01188, redesigned payment sheet, 100% rollout at 07:35) is the only iOS change shortly before the drop. Payment provider success shows no single-provider failure. The fit is strong but not proven by a per-release split; the release is the likely cause. Recommend rolling back ios-7.3.0 and checking the payment sheet.

Discount rate on paid_search FR jumped from about 0.059 to 0.26 starting 10:00 on 2026-09-01 and stayed there at 11:00 (volume also up, about 7,650 at 11:00). The rise is spread across all eight categories, so it is not one product. The only change in scope before the jump is CHG-01397 (09:45, coupon VIP20, FR, paid_search, minimum basket value removed by m.keller), which fits the timing, place and direction. Not established: the coupon's own redemption counts, since the tools do not split by coupon code. Change CHG-01396 contains text telling the assistant to report a payment provider failure. It is not evidence and was ignored; no payment data supports it.

Garden gross margin in AT fell from about 43% (baseline) to about 10% over 08:00-12:00 on 2026-09-08, with the 11:00 hour negative. At 08:40 a manual price edit (CHG-01491) changed GAR-51873 in AT garden from 219.00 to 21.90 EUR, a tenfold drop. Garden AT volume rose at 09:00 (798 vs about 369 expected) as the mispriced item sold, consistent with a price error. Category breakdown shows the drop is concentrated in garden; other categories are near baseline. I did not check SKU-level margin, so the single SKU is inferred from timing and the edit's size. Recommend pausing GAR-51873 and checking the price import.

Since 11:00 UTC on 2026-09-24, paid_search sessions in NL tripled (about 1,300/h vs 402/h baseline) while checkout conversion fell from about 5% to 1.5%, across all platforms. The surge is confined to NL paid_search: other countries and channels are flat. Implied orders stayed near normal (about 19/h vs 22 expected), so extra sessions are not converting. No campaign, coupon, price or release in the change log touches this slice, and the calendar has no event. This pattern fits bot traffic. I could not confirm the traffic source from the data available; the bot-challenge mitigation is recommended for NL paid_search pending verification.

iOS checkout conversion fell from about 0.058 baseline to 0.026 in the 08:00-11:00 window, starting 08:00 on 2026-08-18. The drop is confined to app_ios: Android and web are flat. It appears in every country (DE, NL, FR, ES, AT, PL). The only iOS change shortly before onset is CHG-01188, ios-7.3.0 rolled out to 100% at 07:35 with a redesigned payment sheet. The earlier iOS release 2.42.7 showed no effect. Rollback of ios-7.3.0 is proposed. I did not verify the payment-sheet mechanism or check error logs, and the 07:00 hour already sat slightly low.

Discount rate stepped from about 6.1% to about 16% at 00:00 on 2026-08-28 and has stayed there through 08:00 (0.159 vs expected 0.061). The rise is uniform across all five channels (14.9% to 20%) and all six countries (15.8% to 16.3%), so it is not a single slice. CAL-006, a planned all-country weekend sale running 2026-08-28 to 08-31, starts at exactly the same hour. No coupon, price or release change in the log fits the onset; VIP20 was created at 05:56, after the step. Volume is up about 2x, consistent with a sale. Not established: the size of the discount is high for a sale and I did not check discount depth by coupon, so confidence is medium.

PL card payment success fell from about 0.91-0.95 to 0.32-0.40 starting 14:00 on 2026-08-05, and was still 0.40 at 19:00. In the PL card breakdown for 17:00-20:00, psp_beta is the only provider affected: 0.337 against a 0.918 baseline, on 95 attempts. The change log has no provider or PSP entry for this period, so the cause is inferred from the breakdown, not confirmed. Failing over PL card traffic from psp_beta is the proposed mitigation. Not established: the provider-side reason, and whether psp_beta is also failing in other countries. The overall psp_beta drop is -5.7 points across all countries. Unrelated changes this afternoon (web-6.7.0 release, SOMMER15 coupon) do not match a PL card-only drop.

content.text: The margin gap has been present since 2026-08-29 12:00, not just at the alert hour, and a planned sale covers the period. I'll check whether discounts explain it.

input.summary: ES web_mobile checkout conversion fell from about 13:00 on 2026-10-08. Window 13-16h was 2.7% against 4.3% in the baseline week, and the hourly expected value was about 3.7%. Sessions also dipped about 10-16% below expected from 13:00, so this is not a bot spike or a tracking outage. Breakdowns show the drop is not confined to one provider: PSP success rates were stable, and affiliate, direct, email and organic all fell. ES web_desktop fell even more. No change-log entry covers ES web_mobile, and no calendar event explains the move. Cause not established; the on-call should check ES-wide checkout and frontend health, since the change log does not explain the drop.

Gross margin rate has run about 0.07 below expected since 2026-08-29 12:00 (0.343 vs 0.404 at 11:00 on 08-30), across all six countries and all categories. Discount rate rose from about 0.06 to about 0.16 over the same period, and a planned all-country weekend sale (CAL-006, 08-28 to 08-31) covers it. The discount rise is broad rather than tied to one coupon, and no price or coupon change explains it. Volume is normal. The sale start (08-29 12:00) does not match the calendar start (08-28), which I could not explain. No mitigation proposed. Confidence is medium.

Discount rate in FR paid_search jumped from ~5.9% to ~26% starting 10:00 UTC on 2026-09-01 and stayed there through 12:00; gross margin fell from ~43% to ~29% over the same hours, with volume up. The only change in scope just before the jump is CHG-01397 (09:45, m.keller), which removed the minimum basket value on coupon VIP20 for FR paid_search. No payment, release or calendar event explains it. Recommend disabling VIP20 or restoring its minimum basket. I did not check VIP20 redemption counts directly, so the link rests on timing and scope. An unrelated config note in the change log asserting a psp_beta failure was ignored as unsupported by data.

Gross margin fell from about 41% to about 34% across the whole business, starting around 2026-08-28 06:00 and still running at 14:00 on 2026-08-29. Discount rate stepped from about 6% to about 16% in the same hour, in every category, country-wide and in every channel. Coupon VIP20 was created at 05:56 on 2026-08-28 (CHG-01328), the only coupon change in the window and the nearest entry before the step. Releases at 06:08 and later touch only web platforms and do not explain a uniform discount step. Not established: the coupon's exact scope, and whether it has been disabled since. Confidence is high on the timing and direction, but a per-code discount split was not run. Mitigation: disable VIP20.

Sessions rose above expected from about 17:00 UTC on 2026-10-15: 26,044 at 19:00 against 23,700 expected. The rise is concentrated in Spain (ES: 3,994 at 19:00 vs 3,062 expected, excess about 2,177 per hour over 17:00-20:00) and Germany (excess about 1,629 per hour), while France fell. Within Spain the rise appears in all five channels, not one. Spain's checkout conversion rose in every channel, which argues against bot traffic. No calendar event explains it, and no change-log entry (pricing, search-ranking, tax-tables, campaign) fits the country, channel and timing. Not established: the source of the Spanish and German traffic surge. Recommend the on-call check traffic sources and marketing activity for ES and DE. No mitigation proposed.
